questions.stem: A negative reagent control is most useful for evaluating:

choices.text: Nonspecific signal from detection reagents or endogenous activity
Whether the patient expresses the target

questions.explanation: Omitting or replacing the primary reagent helps reveal nonspecific detection-system or endogenous background.

questions.stem: Both test tissue and positive control are negative in an IHC run. The correct interpretation is:
questions.explanation: A failed positive control invalidates the run because assay performance was not demonstrated.

questions.stem: Heat-induced epitope retrieval should be optimized by changing:

choices.text: Buffer chemistry, pH, temperature, and time in a controlled study

questions.explanation: Retrieval is method-dependent and should be optimized systematically with appropriate controls.

questions.stem: Diffuse brown background on an HRP-DAB stain may be reduced by reviewing:

choices.text: Endogenous peroxidase block, antibody concentration, washing, and detection conditions

questions.explanation: Background can arise from endogenous enzyme activity, excess antibody/detection reagents, inadequate washing, or tissue-related factors.

questions.stem: A chemical fume hood is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Engineering controls reduce exposure at the source and are preferred before relying only on PPE.

questions.stem: To prepare 100 mL of a 10% solution from a 20% stock, the volume of stock required is:
questions.explanation: Using C1V1=C2V2: 20% × V1 = 10% × 100 mL, so V1 = 50 mL.

questions.stem: A stain failure affects every slide after a new reagent lot is introduced. The best first quality action is to:

choices.text: Document, contain affected work, and investigate the lot change
Change several unrelated variables at once

questions.explanation: A systematic response includes containment, documentation, comparison to prior performance, and controlled corrective action.

questions.stem: A corrective action is considered effective when:

choices.text: Follow-up evidence shows the problem does not recur as expected

questions.explanation: Effectiveness checks confirm that the intervention actually controlled the identified problem.

questions.stem: The document that provides hazard, handling, and emergency information for a chemical is the:
questions.explanation: The Safety Data Sheet describes hazards, protective measures, spill response, storage, and other chemical-safety information.

questions.stem: A temperature-controlled instrument repeatedly exceeds limits. The best response is to:

choices.text: Remove or restrict use, assess affected work, and investigate
Average the values until they pass

questions.explanation: Out-of-limit equipment requires containment, impact assessment, documentation, and corrective action before routine use resumes.
